It is drawn as two sloped planes, light on the left and dark on the right, which end in an eave line at row 55 with shadow beneath. A second tiled awning roof at rows 83-97 projects over the shop front and ends in an edge line with shadow. Below are the front faces: cream upper wall with windows, red sign and glass shopfront, about 100 rows in total. The roofs are sloped planes, which counts as evidence (c). The two roof slopes are drawn receding in isometric style, so a side face is visible.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a whole building, the same kind as the references. Its outlines are tinted: dark blue-grey beside the roof and dark brown-red beside the sign, with 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels. That avoids the black-sticker look. The shading and texture are still shallower than the references. The slate roof has about 4 steps with a modest tile pattern, and the cream siding is mostly 2-3 tones of regular stripes with no plaster speckle or grain. The red sign panel, the awning and the dark eave band are broad, nearly flat fills. Measured near-flat coverage is 9%, against 0% for both references. Visible tones per tile are 9, against 12 and 10 for the references, so it is slightly lower. Next to the references' per-tile speckle and per-tile highlights, the candidate looks cleaner and flatter, closer to a vector-like finish. It falls a little short of the Beodeul bar.

A second tiled roof/awning (rows 83-98) projects over the shopfront. The south front face runs from about row 42 to 159 (second floor wall, sign, shopfront). The roof planes and the awning count as top surfaces under evidence (c).

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 9 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, so it is close to the stone reference but below house-h101. Its near-flat coverage is 9% against 0% for both references. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines are tinted (dark blue-grey beside the roof, dark brown beside the sign) and not near-black. The roof has about 4 steps with some tile-row texture, but it is smoother and more uniform than the references' scalloped tiles with per-tile highlights. Overall it is clean and well structured but slightly flatter and less dense than the Beodeul standard, and the 9% flat coverage with shallower shading leaves it short of the bar.

answer.evidence: The building has a large sloped tile roof occupying rows 3-54. Its silhouette widens row by row from 3 to 90 px, and it is split into a light left plane and a dark right plane at a central ridge, which is a hip/gable roof seen from above with a front eave line near row 54 and a shadow below. A second tile-roofed awning (rows 83-98) projects over the shop front and ends in a lighter edge line. Below it are the cream upper wall with windows (rows 42-82) and the ground-floor shop front with sign, noren and display windows, giving a front face well over 3 rows. The roof planes are drawn as receding sloped surfaces, so the object reads as 3/4 view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a whole building like the references, so the kind matches. Its outlines are tinted: dark blue-grey beside the roof, dark brown beside the sign and awning, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral. That is good craft and not the sticker look. The roof has a tile pattern with about 4-5 steps, and the siding has horizontal board lines. The weaknesses are the flat areas. The cream wall is only 2-3 tones with stripes and no plaster speckle or grain. The red sign panel and the dark awning band are large flat blocks. The shop-front door and window glass are simple. Near-flat coverage is 9% against 0% for both references. Visible tones per tile are 9 against 12 and 10, which is slightly lower. The references show per-tile highlights, speckle and stone-by-stone shading, so the candidate sits a step below them in shading depth and surface grain. Pale walls and a clean modern look are not penalised, but the flat fills and shallower ramps leave it a little behind the Beodeul bar, so it fails when in doubt.
